direction: The Acceptable Error: understated 1960s bureaucratic retro-futurism in the spirit of Brazil (film), but original. Industrial gray, slate, blue-gray, cream, muted teal and small restrained signal accents. Smooth flat pixel clusters, deliberate economical colors, clean silhouettes, occasional patched panels, screws and fasteners. NO steampunk brass, gears, leather-bound antiques, fantasy devices, heavy grime, decorative rivet overload, noisy dithering, gradient haze, anti-aliasing or text baked into the interface frame. LOCKED SOURCE DIMENSIONS: main scene backgrounds EXACTLY 314×206 logical pixels, displayed at 4× nearest-neighbor; NPC portraits EXACTLY 564×278 pixels, displayed at 1× with independently composited background and foreground layers when applicable; item inventory icons EXACTLY 96×96 pixels on a transparent canvas, displayed at 1× within the approved slot; item inspection illustrations EXACTLY 565×451 pixels, displayed at 1×. These are production dimensions, not suggestions. Never resize a low-resolution scene into a portrait or inspector illustration. Scene-to-portrait environment pairing: where an NPC conversation occurs, author a separate OPAQUE portrait background at exactly 564×278 that depicts the same physical location as its 314×206 main scene, but with a tighter, more detailed and perspective-consistent camera view. Do not resize, crop, blur, or upscale the main scene to produce this background. Each NPC pose is a distinct TRANSPARENT RGBA PNG foreground, exactly 564×278, with fully transparent pixels outside the sprite (no painted environment and no baked-in background). Independently layer the foreground over the matching opaque portrait background; share that background across every pose at the location. Main scene and paired portrait background should maintain coherent architecture, furniture, lighting and palette, without reproducing identical framing. All artwork is draft-only unless record status is reused or approved.
